_README: ADD OR EDIT MODELS AND KEYS HERE. This is the shipped example: the dashboard copies it to config/providers.json on first run, and that copy is gitignored so your own choices and key names never get pushed. Never put an API key value in either file - only the NAME of the environment variable that holds it. Values live in .env (gitignored, chmod 600). To enable a provider: get a key, paste it into the provider's card in the dashboard (or add the variable to .env yourself), then flip enabled on. Lower priority number is tried first; on quota/429/auth failure the next enabled provider is tried. 'model' is the one in use; 'models' is the catalogue the dashboard (tools/dashboard.py) lets you pick from. status: untested = nobody has verified this model on your key yet, ok = verified working, limited = reachable but quota or capacity restricted, unavailable = not callable at all.

models.description: Newest flash generation and the best quality of the flash tier. Slowest to answer (~30s on a CV) and the most likely to return a temporary 503 under load.
Previous flash generation. Noticeably quicker than 3.8 and quieter under load - the sane default when 3.8 keeps returning 503.
Stable older flash. Still strong at structured JSON, and the most consistently available of the lot.
Lite variant: fastest and cheapest of the 3.5 line, with a shallower grasp of long job descriptions. Good for quick re-runs.
Older lite model kept as a low-latency fallback. Weakest rewriting quality here - fine for smoke tests, not for a CV you will send.
Preview build of the 3.0 flash line. Works, but a preview model can be withdrawn without notice.
Floating alias that always points at the current flash model. Convenient, but it moves under you and is the first alias to get rate-limited at peak.
Floating alias for the current flash-lite model. Same moving-target caveat, lower demand.
Pro tier - the strongest reasoning available on AI Studio. A free key will usually get 429 quota-exceeded here; it wants a billed project.
Retired. Google returns 404 'no longer available to new users'. Kept here only so an old config pointing at it is explained rather than mysterious.

The strongest model available on Groq for heavy tasks, structured JSON extraction, and reasoning, supporting up to 500 tokens per second.
The fastest text model on the platform (~1000 tokens per second), optimized for routing and rapid completions.
Available in preview, this model provides excellent multilingual capabilities and strong performance in structured data extraction.
Safety-classifier sibling of gpt-oss-20b. Built to judge content against a policy, not to write prose - wrong tool for tailoring a CV.
A highly accurate and efficient audio transcription model giving up to 8 hours (28,800 seconds) of free processing daily. Audio only - it has no chat endpoint, so it cannot tailor a CV.
A highly capable, large-scale general assistant model running at roughly 280 tokens per second. Decommissioned by Groq - it no longer appears on current accounts.
The highest-volume free option, allowing up to 500,000 tokens per day at blindingly fast inference speeds (~560 tokens per second). Decommissioned by Groq - it no longer appears on current accounts.
DeepSeek's general chat model. Cheap, solid at structured JSON, and the sensible OpenRouter default.
Free Gemini flash routed through OpenRouter. Useful as a no-cost fallback when the direct AI Studio key is rate-limited.
Large open-weight general assistant. Slower than the flash models but strong at following a long tailoring brief.
Strong multilingual open-weight model with reliable structured output - a good second opinion when a rewrite reads flat.

_LIMITS_README: USAGE BARS. 'usage_probe' says how the dashboard asks a provider for its real numbers: groq_headers = read x-ratelimit-* off a completion (real limit and remaining, per model, but it costs one request); openrouter_key = GET /key, free, account-wide credits; gemini_none = Google AI Studio has no quota endpoint, so nothing can be read. 'limits' is the fallback denominator used when no probe exists - the dashboard counts calls made from this tool (state/usage.jsonl) against it and labels it 'declared'. Keys: rpm/rpd = requests per minute/day, tpm/tpd = tokens per minute/day. Omit a key you do not know rather than guessing; a model block may carry its own 'limits' to override the provider's. Groq's numbers below were read off live headers; Gemini's are the usual free-tier shape and you should correct them against your own AI Studio console.
